'''John T. Markert''' is a professor in [[The University of Texas at Austin]] [[University of Texas at Austin College of Natural Sciences|physics department]] and was department chair from 2005 to 2009. His group has done extensive research on high temperature superconducting materials, high-q oscillator experiments, dynamics of [[Ferromagnetism|ferromagnets]], [[Magnetic resonance imaging|nuclear magnetic resonance microscopy]] and [[spectroscopy]], and optically switchable metal hydride films.<ref>[http://www.ph.utexas.edu/~markweb/PEOPLE/people_main.htm Magnetism and Superconductivity Group ]</ref>  A textbook written by Dr. Markert and Hans Ohanian, ''Physics for Engineers and Scientists,'' was released in 2008 by Norton Publishers.<ref name="isbn0-393-97422-7">{{cite book |author1=John Markert |author2=Ohanian, Hans C. |title=Physics for Engineers and Scientists, Regular Edition |publisher=W. W. Norton |location=New York |year=2006 |isbn=0-393-97422-7 }}</ref> The book is for a [[Calculus|calculus-based]] introductory course.  As of 2008 his H ([[Hirsch number]]) index is 30.{{Citation needed|date=June 2008}}.

Markert was born in the Bronx in 1957, the youngest of seven.  He attended Regis High School, an all male, all scholarship Jesuit high school.  Afterward, he did his undergraduate study at [[Bowdoin College]] in Brunswick, Maine. He received his graduate degree at [[Cornell University]] in Ithaca, New York, and did post-graduate work at the [[University of California, San Diego]] under Brian Maple. He was shortly afterward recruited by UT Austin to be an assistant professor in 1990.{{citation needed|date=October 2017}}
